L53: > Le rôle de l’écriture n’est pas de consigner les résultats d’une recherche, mais bien le processus même de la recherche.
L54: >
L55: > Récoltes et Semailles, A. Grothendieck
L56: Addressing A. Grothendieck’s extensive body of published works involves key considerations. Initially, while Grothendieck’s mathematical and literary reflections spanned his entire life, it was only the active period from 1950 to 1969 that saw traditional forms of regular publication. Post this phase, publishing his works became sporadic and complex. Additionally, at present, a wealth of unpublished material holds potential for posthumous publication.
L57: With these aspects in focus, the CSG is committed to enhancing accessibility and collaborating with publishing houses to effectively study, catalog and enlarge A. Grothendieck’s body of published works. This endeavor aims to formally categorize and grant citability to all of Grothendieck’s publications in a unified fashion.
L58: While more sophisticated readers who are familiar with Grothendieck’s main contributions will be most interested in the unpublished works, even within the realm of these published works, their classifications, and posthumous additions, these experts might come across novel or less familiar items.
L59: Furthermore, by meticulously compiling Grothendieck’s entire body of publications in categories, we offer readers the opportunity to place his works within contexts of interest, thus fostering potential avenues for new research.
